Gian Antonio Grassi (1775–1849) was an Italian Jesuit priest, scholar, and missionary who played a significant role in the early history of the Catholic Church in the United States. Here’s a detailed overview of his life and contributions:

### **Early Life and Education**
- Born on **June 17, 1775**, in **Milan, Italy**, Grassi joined the **Society of Jesus (Jesuits)** in **1793** at a time when the order was suppressed in many parts of Europe.
- He studied philosophy and theology, becoming a professor of rhetoric and later of mathematics and physics.

### **Missionary Work in the United States**
- In **1810**, Grassi was sent to the United States as part of the Jesuit mission to re-establish the order in the New World.
- He arrived in **Georgetown, Washington D.C.**, where he became a professor at **Georgetown College** (now Georgetown University).
- He taught **mathematics, physics, and astronomy**, and also served as the college’s **prefect of studies** (1812–1815).

### **Founding of Gonzaga College**
- In **1821**, Grassi was instrumental in founding **Gonzaga College** (now Gonzaga University) in **Spokane, Washington**, though the school was not formally established until later.
- He also helped establish **St. Mary’s College** in **Kentucky** (1822), which later became **St. Mary’s College of Kentucky** (now defunct).

### **Diplomatic and Ecclesiastical Roles**
- Grassi served as a key intermediary between the **Jesuits in America** and the **Vatican**.
- He was appointed **Vice-Provincial of the Jesuit Mission in the United States** (1819–1822).
- In **1823**, he was sent to **Rome** to negotiate the restoration of the Jesuit order in the U.S., which had been suppressed in 1773. His efforts contributed to the eventual re-establishment of the Jesuits in America.

### **Later Life and Death**
- After returning to Italy, Grassi continued his work in education and administration.
- He died on **December 10, 1849**, in **Rome, Italy**.

### **Legacy**
- Grassi is remembered as a key figure in the **revival of Jesuit education in the United States**.
- His efforts helped strengthen Catholic institutions in America during a critical period of growth.
- **Gonzaga University** and **Georgetown University** honor his contributions to their foundations.
